sections.title: What you need to be able to do
sections.content: Solve a pair of simultaneous equations where one is linear (a straight line) and one is quadratic (a curve), using substitution. Each pair has two answer points — find both, and give each as an (x, y) pair.

sections.title: Method steps — keep this in view
sections.content:
Method steps — refer back to this while you work:

- Step 1: Make y the subject of the straight-line (linear) equation.
- Step 2: Substitute that into the curve (quadratic) equation.
- Step 3: Move everything to one side so the equation equals 0.
- Step 4: Solve the quadratic — factorise, or use the formula.
- Step 5: Put each x back in to find its y. Write your answers in pairs and check them.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content:
Solve:  y = x² − 2x + 3   and   y = x + 3

Step 1–2: The line already gives y, so substitute:  x² − 2x + 3 = x + 3
Step 3: Move to one side:  x² − 3x = 0
Step 4: Factorise:  x(x − 3) = 0  →  x = 0 or x = 3
Step 5: Find y from y = x + 3:  when x = 0, y = 3;  when x = 3, y = 6

Answers:  (0, 3)  and  (3, 6)

sections.title: Question 7
sections.content:

   x² + y² = 9          and          y = x + 1

sections.title: Question 8
sections.content:
A rectangle has an area of 12 cm² and a perimeter of 14 cm.

By forming and solving a pair of simultaneous equations, find the length and width of the rectangle.
